services.title: Data, AI and advisory

about_page.title: Sixteen years of understanding how Mozambique communicates.
about_page.lead: Playground was founded in Maputo in 2010. Today we are a multidisciplinary team of more than thirty people working with national and international organisations across the country.
story: We started as a creative and events company. Over time our clients asked us for more: to help them understand their audiences, manage their reputation and engage communities, government and partners.

That is the direction we continue to build. Playground connects stakeholder intelligence, strategic communication and high quality execution, because in Mozambique relationships, trust and context often decide outcomes as much as the message itself.

insights.title: Why stakeholder intelligence should sit closer to strategy.
insights.excerpt: Communication teams often see signals early. The question is whether those signals are interpreted before the decision is made.
body: In most organisations, the communication team is one of the first places where signals arrive. A journalist asks an unexpected question. A community leader raises the same concern for the third time. A regulator changes tone in a meeting. A partner stops replying as quickly as before.
Individually these look like operational details. Together they often describe a shift in how the organisation is perceived, and in what stakeholders expect from it.

The problem is that these signals are usually handled as communication tasks: answer the journalist, prepare a statement, schedule a meeting. They rarely reach the table where strategic decisions are made, at least not in a structured way and not early enough.

Stakeholder intelligence is the discipline of collecting those signals, interpreting them and presenting them to leadership in a form that supports decisions. It is not a report of media coverage. It is an answer to a simple question: what is changing in our environment, and what does it mean for what we are about to do?

Three practical steps make a difference. First, agree which stakeholders and issues really matter for the next twelve months. Second, create a regular rhythm where signals from media, field teams and relationships are brought together and discussed. Third, connect that discussion to specific decisions, not to general awareness.

In complex operating environments such as Mozambique, where formal structures do not always show how influence works, this matters even more. The organisations that read their environment well are usually the ones that avoid surprises.

cases.title: A stakeholder programme for a major energy project.
cases.summary: Mapping, engagement and reporting for a project with national visibility and local impact.
cases.challenge: The project had many audiences with very different expectations: central government, provincial authorities, host communities, suppliers, media and international partners. Information was fragmented across teams and leadership lacked a single view of where relationships stood.
cases.approach: We started with a structured stakeholder map built from interviews with the client's field and corporate teams, media analysis and our own network knowledge. Each stakeholder group received a clear objective, an owner and a rhythm of engagement. We then set up a monthly intelligence brief connecting what we were hearing to the decisions leadership was preparing.
delivered: Twelve month engagement plan with owners
Daily media monitoring in Portuguese and English

results.label: shared view of stakeholders across teams

cases.quote: For the first time we could see, in one place, where every important relationship stood.

cases.title: A national campaign that spoke to every province.
cases.summary: Concept, production and rollout of a multichannel campaign for a mobile operator.
cases.challenge: The brand needed a campaign that would feel relevant in Maputo and in rural districts, across age groups and languages, while supporting a specific commercial objective.
cases.approach: We tested the core idea with small groups in three provinces before production. The final concept used real people and places, with versions adapted for radio, outdoor, digital and activations. Media was planned to balance national reach with local presence.
delivered: Outdoor and point of sale materials

cases.title: Rebuilding media confidence for a financial institution.
cases.summary: Press office, spokesperson preparation and issues management over twelve months.
cases.challenge: After a period of negative coverage, the institution had become cautious with the media. Journalists found it difficult to get answers and stories were often published without the bank's view.
cases.approach: We proposed a more open but well prepared approach. We agreed a small group of spokespeople, trained them, created a calendar of positive stories and set clear response times for media questions. Monitoring helped us see quickly which issues were growing.

cases.title: An international conference delivered end to end.
cases.summary: Concept, logistics, protocol and content for a high level gathering in Maputo.
cases.challenge: A two day conference with government, donors, civil society and international delegations, organised in a short timeframe and with strict protocol requirements.
cases.approach: One project lead coordinated venue, suppliers, protocol, accreditation, interpretation, design and content. We built a detailed run of show, rehearsed critical moments with the client and kept a daily coverage team on site.
